title: Approval ladder + technical preflight with Mirella Financial
next_steps: Send redlined MSA and DPA by EOD 2026-09-02
Share infra preflight checklist and network diagram
Schedule technical pilot kickoff with infra and SE (aim for week of 2026-09-07)
action_items: Asha Patel - circulate MSA redline draft - 2026-09-02
Evan Cho - deliver benchmark spreadsheet + KMS integration notes - 2026-09-04
Miguel Torres - confirm VPC peering constraints and egress allowances - 2026-09-03
summary: Intake call to map Mirella's internal approval ladder, align on MSA/DPA redlines, and run a technical preflight for a reserved-capacity pilot. Customer emphasized strict KMS controls and data residency. Agreed next steps: redlines, infra checklist, and pilot kickoff scheduling.
topics: SLA tiers, uptime targets and crediting
KMS / HSM expectations and key custody model
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-31 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 48 min | Attendees: Asha (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Daniel (Mirella Procurement), Priya (Mirella Legal), Miguel (Mirella Infra)

[00:00] Asha Patel: hey everybody, thanks for joining on time, i'm Asha from Redwood, and i'll run us through the agenda real quick, want to make sure we capture the approval path and then do a quick infra preflight so evan can ask the right questions.
[00:20] Daniel Ruiz: yep, thanks, Asha. we have a short window so i'll try to be brief. procurement wants to understand the MSA exceptions and DPA constraints before i push this up the ladder. our CFO needs a clear pricing path and sla commitments.
[00:40] Priya Sharma: hi, Priya here, legal — i'll focus on data residency, data retention, and the DPA language around subprocessors. also we need to know whether keys live in our KMS or Redwood's HSM.
[01:05] Evan Cho: thanks Priya, quick note — Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS and our managed key flow; we usually detail that in the security pack. for dedicated/private deployments we can do customer KMS with BYOK and even integrate with HSM via standard KMIP flows, but there are ops implications.
[01:30] Miguel Torres: ops implications = more ops on our side? can you clarify the network egress and peering expectations? our security team is strict about cross-account peering.
[01:50] Evan Cho: good question — for VPC deployment (Redwood Private) we support VPC peering and private link. egress charges depend on region and whether you use our hosted mesh; we'll send a network diagram. also need to call out that some model variants might be served in dedicated pools and that could mean cross-subnet flows.
[02:20] Daniel Ruiz: timeline — procurement wants a clear route: if legal signs off and finance approves pricing, we can greenlight pilot. who typically signs the MSA at Redwood?
[02:40] Asha Patel: we have a standard AE-driven process — AE coordinates, legal signs the MSA and finance signs the PO. for larger Dedicated deals there's an enterprise contract owner, but i'll be your point.
[03:00] Priya Sharma: on subprocessors, do you have a list? also we need SOC2 type II and a statement on data at rest encryption.
[03:25] Evan Cho: yes, we'll share the current subprocessor list. SOC 2 Type II is in our package. encryption at rest is AES-256 by default, and for customer-managed keys we can show proof of key custody — note, sometimes the naming in our docs gets mangled by old exports, so i'll attach the security pack link in the follow-up.
[03:50] Miguel Torres: what about egress logging and audit trails? we need tamper-evident logs for inference requests for compliance.
[04:10] Evan Cho: we emit audit logs with request IDs and we can retain at configurable retention windows; for an air-gapped/private on-prem install we can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloudwatch, depending on the environment.
[04:40] Asha Patel: quick pause — i want to map approvals: procurement (Daniel) -> legal (Priya) -> finance (CFO) -> security sign-off (Miguel's team) -> final PO. is that accurate?
[05:00] Daniel Ruiz: yes that's the ladder, though security might loop in external audit folks. 
[05:15] Evan Cho: can i ask about expected throughput during pilot? that'll impact which nodes we recommend.
[05:30] Miguel Torres: pilot is small to start — roughly 10 QPS sustained, spikes to 60 for short periods. latency target is 150-200ms 95p for short prompts.
[05:50] Evan Cho: 10 QPS sustained with 60 peak fits a small Dedicated pool; latency target of 150-200ms is doable for trimmed sequence lengths and choosing a low-latency model. i'll note that quantization and batching configs affect latency/cost tradeoffs.
[06:20] Priya Sharma: on the DPA, our legal team wants deletion guarantees for any PII ingested; can you commit to delete-on-demand or do you retain for model improvement?
[06:45] Evan Cho: out-of-the-box hosted model training is disabled for customers by default; we retain telemetry for SRE but we can scope data retention windows and offer deletion on demand when required in contract. we'll need to flag any exceptions internally.
[07:05] Daniel Ruiz: finance question — how is pricing structured during pilot? is it pay-as-you-go or reserved? we need a predictable number for CFO.
[07:25] Asha Patel: pilots are usually usage-based with a committed cap. we can provide an estimated spend sheet and a short term reserved quote for pilot months to give predictability. Evan will share a benchmark and cost model.
[07:45] Evan Cho: i'll include token-level cost breakdown and expected cost per 1k requests at the pilot profile.
[08:00] Miguel Torres: i want to clarify network flow again, if we do VPC peering, does traffic traverse public internet at any point?
[08:20] Evan Cho: no, with VPC peering or private link the traffic stays on carrier backbone. only if you choose hosted public endpoints would there be internet egress.
[08:40] Priya Sharma: any export control or data residency flags? our clients in EU require EU-only residency. can Redwood pin model serving to a specific region?
[09:05] Evan Cho: yes, we can pin to a region for Dedicated/Private. for Hosted API we have region routing policies, but we recommend Dedicated for strict residency guarantees. we'll include a note about EU-only hosting options.
[09:30] Asha Patel: i'm going to list typical redline asks we see: liability cap tweaks, deletion language in DPA, subprocessors clarity, and SLA credits on downtime. Priya, is that in line with your expectations?
[09:50] Priya Sharma: yes correct. also want indemnity carveouts for regulated data.
[10:05] Evan Cho: just to call out — our standard SLA has a 99.5% uptime for Dedicated with credits in the agreement. Hosted tiers differ. We can quantify the SLOs per-route in the addendum.
[10:30] Miguel Torres: on KMS, we prefer bringing our own keys (BYOK) and having HSM-backed keys. does the Redwood deploy support KMIP or Cloud KMS such as AWS or GCP customer KMS?
[10:50] Evan Cho: we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS; for HSM-backed custodied keys we do a bridge via KMIP for on-prem HSMs or you can use AWS CloudHSM in your account. we'll log the exact integration pathways in the infra preflight doc.
[11:15] Daniel Ruiz: what approvals do you need from us to start a pilot? is legal sign-off on DPA enough or do you need the PO first?
[11:35] Asha Patel: typically DPA and MSA signed is enough for a pilot that uses sandboxed dedicated capacity; for production provisioning we need the PO and payment terms. we'll be flexible for pilot terms.
[11:50] Evan Cho: can i ask for a quick readout from Miguel about their existing infra—what cloud, VPC CIDR, any transit gateways?
[12:05] Miguel Torres: we run on AWS, accounts are separated per environment, VPC CIDR ranges are a mix, we use Transit Gateway in prod. we have strict egress controls and a central KMS in org account.
[12:30] Evan Cho: ok transit gateway is fine, we'll need to map routes and ensure there's no overlapping CIDR with Redwood's peering endpoints. i'll add a checklist item.
[12:45] [brief crosstalk — someone drops and rejoins]
[13:10] Asha Patel: i want to record the decision points: 1) pilot parameters (throughput, latency) 2) legal redlines 3) KMS approach 4) network architecture confirmation. does that sound right?
[13:25] Daniel Ruiz: yes. 
[13:35] Priya Sharma: one more question — if we ask for modifications to the DPA to include stronger deletion rights, how long does redline negotiation typically take?
[13:55] Asha Patel: depends on the asks; small DPA tweaks move quickly (1-2 weeks), deeper indemnity or escrow asks may take longer. we'll flag anything that needs legal escalation.
[14:15] Evan Cho: technical note — for 60 QPS peaks, we recommend a dedicated pool sized for peaks or autoscale with small warmers; warm KV cache is important if you're doing chat-style continuations.
[14:40] Miguel Torres: KV cache = key-value cache? is that stored in our account or Redwood's?
[14:55] Evan Cho: it's part of the runtime; for Private deployments we can configure cache locality and ensure caches sit within your VPC so the data never leaves your network boundary. in hosted modes it's in Redwood's environment but encrypted.
[15:20] Daniel Ruiz: procurement wants explicit rollback and termination terms in case of a breach. can you summarize the standard termination assistance you provide?
[15:40] Asha Patel: we include a termination assistance clause for migration help and a data export process; specifics can be tailored. we'll include timeframes for data export and any fees if applicable.
[16:00] Priya Sharma: please include a sample SLA credit calculation in the follow-up, legal needs to see the math.
[16:15] Evan Cho: noted — i'll include the formula and an example.
[16:30] [pause — brief private chat among redwood folks audible]
[17:10] Miguel Torres: we will run a quick security questionnaire (RFI) — what's the typical turnaround? our security team expects responses in 5 business days.
[17:30] Asha Patel: we aim for 3-5 business days. for deeper pen-test evidence it may take longer, but we'll triage.
[17:50] Daniel Ruiz: on pricing approvals, do you have a standard pilot credit or discount for enterprise pilots? our CFO asks for a capped spend.
[18:05] Asha Patel: yes, we often provide pilot credits or a short-term reserved discount for the pilot months; we'll propose numbers in the follow-up.
[18:20] Evan Cho: i'll share a sample benchmark with cost vs latency tradeoffs — e.g., model A: lower cost higher latency, model B: higher cost lower latency.
[18:40] Priya Sharma: what about audit rights—do we get any on-prem access or are you only offering audit reports?
[19:00] Evan Cho: audit reports (SOC2) and live audits for Dedicated/private are possible under NDA. on-prem deployments allow for more direct audit access.
[19:20] Daniel Ruiz: any blockers you foresee that might delay procurement route?
[19:35] Asha Patel: main blockers we've seen: unusual indemnity asks, offshore data flow concerns, or bespoke key custody requirements. none are showstoppers, just negotiation items.
[19:55] Miguel Torres: are there any bandwidth or peering IP ranges we should whitelist now to avoid delays?
[20:12] Evan Cho: yes — we'll send a short allowlist with IP ranges and FQDNs. also a short doc on expected TLS certs and SNI.
[20:30] [timestamp jump to 30:05 — later in call, clarifying redlines]
[30:05] Priya Sharma: regarding liability cap, would Redwood consider carving out regulatory fines from the cap? our legal team typically asks that.
[30:30] Asha Patel: we can discuss carveouts; need to route that to our legal and exec team. it's not uncommon to see limited carveouts for gross negligence or willful misconduct, but regulatory fines carveouts vary.
[31:00] Daniel Ruiz: okay if we push an initial DPA redline by tomorrow will that speed the review?
[31:15] Asha Patel: yes please. early redlines help us scope negotiations.
[31:30] Evan Cho: one more technical callout — if you need EU-only residency we recommend provisioning a Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1 and pinning the model, this avoids cross-region cache misses.
[31:55] Miguel Torres: that sounds good. what's the expected lead time to stand up a Dedicated pilot cluster?
[32:10] Evan Cho: typically 5-10 business days once contract and PO are in place; if urgent we can prioritize but it may introduce a fee. for pilots we sometimes reuse existing pools to shorten start time.
[32:40] [slight interruption — someone joins late and asks a question about monitoring]
[33:00] New Speaker (Speaker 5): how do you surface per-route latency and cost in the console?
[33:15] Evan Cho: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards showing tokens, latency histograms, and cost per token. we can export reports or give read-only console access to your FinOps.
[33:40] Priya Sharma: please add that FinOps access is in the follow-up.
[33:50] Asha Patel: noted.
[34:05] Daniel Ruiz: to recap — procurement wants MSA/DPA redlines, finance wants a capped pilot cost, security wants KMS BYOK and network allowlist, infra wants a clear lead time for Dedicated cluster and peering details.
[34:25] Priya Sharma: legal also needs deletion language and subprocessors list.
[34:40] Evan Cho: i'll package the infra preflight, benchmark, and security pack.
[34:55] Asha Patel: action items: Evan sends infra + benchmarks, Asha sends MSA/DPA redline template, Miguel sends CIDR and transit gateway info, Daniel will route redlines to procurement ladder.
[35:20] Miguel Torres: i'll gather the VPC range and send a short doc by 2026-09-03.
[35:35] Daniel Ruiz: i'll aim to circulate internal approval ladder and tentative CFO signoff date by 2026-09-01.
[35:50] Asha Patel: ok, let's pick a pilot kickoff week tentatively 2026-09-07 pending paperwork.
[36:05] Priya Sharma: one more micro-item — please include SLA credit math and sample DPA redline in the email.
[36:20] Evan Cho: will do.
[36:40] [closing minutes — logistics and doc links shared]
[42:10] Asha Patel: i'll share links to the security pack, sample MSA/DPA redlines, and an infra checklist in the follow-up email. links: MSA draft (link), DPA draft (link), security pack (link), infra checklist (link).
[42:40] Daniel Ruiz: thanks all, this was useful.
[42:55] Priya Sharma: thanks, look forward to the docs.
[43:10] Evan Cho: thanks, we'll get everything over within two business days.
[43:25] Asha Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up and schedule the pilot kickoff when approvals are complete.
[47:20] [call ends]
